publishing.description:
Someone asks how much you sold by region. Then by product. Then by month. You can write a formula for every question, or you can build one PivotTable and answer all of them.

Excel PivotTables and Dashboards for Absolute Beginners is a plain-English guide to doing exactly that. Instead of long chapters, you get 77 short lessons, one idea per page, each with a clear diagram of what is happening and one small thing to try before you move on.

Inside, you'll learn how to:
- Check that your data has the shape a PivotTable needs, and tidy it if it doesn't
- Insert your first PivotTable and understand the Field List and its four boxes
- Put fields in rows, columns and values, and change what gets added up
- Sort, filter and keep only the top items
- Group dates into months, quarters and weeks, and numbers into bands
- Show values as shares, ranks, running totals and changes, without writing a formula
- Add a calculated field, look behind a number, and keep the table fresh
- Find out why a PivotTable gives the wrong answer, and fix it
- Add PivotCharts, slicers and a timeline
- Lay out a one-page dashboard, print it on one page and check it before you send it

The practice pages all use the same small example, a corner shop's year of sales, so you are always working on something real.

It helps if you can already type data into Excel and add up a column. If you have read Excel for Absolute Beginners, you are ready. No unexplained jargon.

By the last page you'll be able to turn a long list of rows into answers, and the answers into one page someone else can use.
publishing.audience: Excel users who can type data and use SUM, and want to summarise it without a formula for every question.
